lead: Arlington plumbing deals with clay soil, slab foundations and homes from the 1970s and 1980s growth years. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Arlington.
risk: slab leaks from shifting clay, aging water heaters and burst pipes in hard freezes
risk_short: slab leaks, water heaters and frozen pipes
why: Arlington grew fast in the 1970s and 1980s, so many homes are 40 to 50 years old. Their copper lines under the slab and cast-iron drains are aging, and the city's expansive clay moves with every drought and wet spell.
Rare hard freezes, like February 2021, burst attic and exterior-wall pipes. Many water heaters from the original builds have been replaced once and are due again.
water: Arlington Water Utilities treats water from Lake Arlington and from reservoirs supplied through the Tarrant Regional Water District. The water is moderately hard.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Replace water heaters past 10 to 15 years.
Know where your main shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Arlington, the Entertainment District, Viridian, North, East and Southwest Arlington and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Arlington Planning and Development Services, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Why do Arlington homes get slab leaks?
faq.a: Arlington sits on expansive clay that swells when wet and shrinks when dry. That movement stresses copper lines under the slab. Warm floor spots and a running meter are common signs.
